title: Who Is Really Leading the Green-Energy Transition?
summary: Five measures of renewable leadership show why scale, capacity per person, system penetration and trajectory produce different—but complementary—leaders.
key_takeaway: A useful green-energy comparison begins by matching the metric to the decision; no single ranking can capture scale, depth and momentum at once.

inline_figures.caption: Renewable generating capacity per person in 2020 brings smaller hydro-rich and fast-building systems into view.
Renewables as a share of primary energy in 2020 measures system penetration rather than electricity volume alone.
Country-by-year renewable electricity reveals distinct trajectories beneath the latest-year totals.
Clustering average renewable-electricity trajectories separates scale leaders, steady growers and lower-output pathways.
